Knead the semolina, flour, salt and water for 10 minutes into a smooth soft dough and rest 30 minutes.
Cook the onions slowly in 3 tbsp oil for 15 minutes, add the garlic, tomatoes, harissa and spices and cook for 15 minutes until thick.
Divide the dough into 6, oil the surface and stretch each piece paper-thin.
Spread filling in the middle and fold into squares.
Cook on a hot griddle for 3 minutes per side, brush with butter and serve warm.
1 tsp for the dough, the rest for dusting and the tea
Mix the flour, yeast, 1 tsp sugar, salt and water into a sticky dough and beat for 5 minutes.
Cover and leave to rise for 90 minutes until doubled.
With wet hands, pull off balls, poke a hole through the middle and stretch into rings.
Fry at 180°C for 2 minutes per side until puffed and golden, then dust with sugar.
Brew the tea with mint and sugar and serve with the warm sfenj.
Mix the beef with half the onion, parsley, egg, half the garlic, cinnamon, pepper and salt.
Mound the filling on the artichoke bottoms and press on lightly.
Soften the remaining onion and garlic in the oil and butter, add 500 ml water, the chickpeas and salt.
Lay the artichokes in the sauce, cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add the lemon juice and simmer 5 minutes more, then serve with bread.
Make a soft dough with the semolina, water and salt, roll thin and cook as flat rounds in a dry pan for 2 minutes per side, then tear into small pieces.
Brown the chicken with the onions in the oil, add the tomato paste, harissa and spices.
Add 1.2 l water, the potatoes and chickpeas and simmer for 35 minutes, adding the zucchini for the last 10.
Steam the torn bread for 10 minutes and toss with the butter and some broth.
Pile the bread on a platter and top with the chicken, vegetables and plenty of sauce.
Marinate the beef with garlic, spices, half the oil and salt for 20 minutes.
Layer the potatoes, onion and tomatoes in a baking tray and tuck the beef between them.
Mix the tomato paste with 300 ml water and pour over with the remaining oil.
Cover with foil and bake at 190°C for 60 minutes.
Uncover, bake 20 minutes more until golden and sprinkle with parsley.
Rub the semolina with 1 tsp salt and 3 tbsp oil, add the water and knead to a soft dough, then rest 20 minutes.
Brown the beef and onion in the remaining oil, add the tomato paste, spices and 800 ml water and simmer for 60 minutes.
Add the carrots and potatoes and cook for 25 minutes.
Pat the dough into two rounds 1 cm thick, prick and cook in a dry heavy pan for 6 minutes per side.
Serve the kesra in wedges with the stew and coriander.
rechta or fresh thin ribbon noodles
Cook the chicken with the onions, cinnamon, pepper, oil, butter and salt for 10 minutes without browning.
Add 1.5 l water and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add the turnips and chickpeas and cook for 15 minutes.
Steam the noodles over the broth for 10 minutes, toss with a ladle of broth and steam again for 5 minutes.
Serve the noodles topped with chicken and vegetables and broth poured over.
Brown the lamb with the onion and celery in the oil.
Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, spices, half the coriander and salt and cook for 5 minutes.
Add 1.5 l water and simmer for 40 minutes.
Add the frik and chickpeas and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Finish with the remaining coriander and mint and serve with lemon.
Cook the chicken with the onion, half the garlic, spices, olive oil and salt for 10 minutes.
Add 500 ml water and simmer for 35 minutes.
Fry the zucchini in the vegetable oil until golden and drain.
Crush the remaining garlic with the vinegar and stir into the sauce.
Add the zucchini and simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce is thick.
Soften the onions in the oil, add the tomato paste, harissa and spices, then 1.5 l water, carrots and turnips and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the zucchini and chickpeas and simmer 15 minutes.
Grill the merguez for 8 minutes, turning, until charred.
Steam the couscous twice over the broth, fluffing between, and rub in the butter.
Serve the couscous with the merguez, vegetables and broth.
Cook the chicken with the onion, garlic, turmeric, pepper, oil and salt for 10 minutes.
Add 600 ml water and the carrots and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and olives and simmer for 15 minutes.
Whisk the flour with the lemon juice and a little sauce and stir in to thicken.
Simmer 5 minutes and finish with parsley.
Brown the lamb with the onions in the oil, add the tomato paste and spices, then 2 l water and simmer for 60 minutes.
Add the carrots, turnips and cabbage and cook for 20 minutes.
Add the zucchini, pumpkin and chickpeas and cook for 15 minutes.
Steam the couscous over the broth twice, fluffing between, and rub in the butter.
Serve the couscous mounded with lamb and vegetables, with broth on the side.
Fry the beef and onion with cinnamon, pepper and salt for 8 minutes and cool.
Mix with the potato, cheese and parsley.
Place a line of filling on each pastry sheet, fold in the sides and roll into cigars, sealing with egg.
Fry in hot oil for 2 minutes per side until golden.
Drain and serve warm with lemon or soup.
Cook the lamb with the onions, cinnamon, saffron, butter and salt for 10 minutes.
Add 600 ml water, cover and simmer for 75 minutes.
Add the prunes, raisins and honey and simmer for 20 minutes until syrupy.
Stir in the orange blossom water and serve topped with almonds.
Cook the meat with the onion, spices, oil and salt for 10 minutes, add the tomato paste.
Add 1.2 l water and simmer for 45 minutes.
Toast the pasta in the butter until golden.
Add the pasta and chickpeas to the broth and simmer for 12 minutes until tender and saucy.
Serve with the meat and halved eggs on top.
Whisk the chickpea flour with the water, oil, salt and half the cumin until smooth and rest 30 minutes.
Whisk in the eggs and pour into an oiled baking dish.
Bake at 200°C for 40 minutes until set with a golden top.
Cool slightly and cut into squares.
Serve tucked into baguette with harissa and the remaining cumin.
Whisk the chickpea flour, water, oil, salt and cumin until smooth and leave 1 hour.
Pour into a greased tray about 3 cm deep.
Bake at 200°C for 45 minutes until firm and golden on top.
Slice and serve warm with harissa.
Mix the beef with onion, parsley, half the cumin and caraway and salt and roll into small balls.
Cook the garlic in the oil, add the tomatoes, paprika and remaining spices and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the meatballs, cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the peppers, tomatoes, spices, harissa and salt and simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Make four wells and crack in the eggs.
Cover and cook for 5 minutes until the whites are set.
Serve in the pan with crusty bread.
Rub the lamb with ras el hanout, cinnamon, saffron and salt.
Cook with the onions and butter for 10 minutes.
Add 700 ml water, cover and simmer for 2 hours.
Add the raisins, almonds and honey and cook for 25 minutes until thick and glossy.
Mix the lamb with onion, spices and salt and shape into small balls.
Grill or pan-fry the kebabs for 8 minutes until browned.
Simmer the cherries with pomegranate molasses, sugar, butter and 100 ml water for 10 minutes.
Add the kebabs and simmer for 5 minutes.
Serve on torn pita with parsley and toasted pine nuts.
juiced, half for the garlic sauce
Marinate the chicken in yogurt, crushed garlic, tomato paste, paprika, lemon juice and salt for 1 hour.
Make toum by blending the peeled garlic with salt, then drizzling in the oil and lemon juice slowly until thick and white.
Thread the chicken on skewers and grill for 12 minutes.
Add the chicken, pickles and parsley, roll tightly and toast briefly.
Mix the rice, tomatoes, onion, herbs, molasses, spice, half the oil, half the lemon juice and salt.
Roll a teaspoon of filling in each leaf.
Line a pot with potato slices and pack the rolls tightly on top.
Pour over the remaining oil, lemon juice and water just to cover, weigh down with a plate and simmer for 50 minutes.
Cool in the pot and serve at room temperature.
Simmer the chicken with the onion and salt in 1.5 l water for 35 minutes, shred and keep the broth.
Fry the vermicelli in 1 tbsp oil until golden, add the rice and 600 ml broth and cook for 18 minutes.
Fry the garlic, fresh and ground coriander in the remaining oil until fragrant.
Simmer the molokhia in 900 ml broth for 10 minutes, then stir in the garlic mixture and chicken.
Brown the beef with the onion in the oil, add the tomato paste and spice.
Add 800 ml water and simmer for 60 minutes.
Add the beans and simmer for 20 minutes.
Fry the garlic and coriander and stir into the stew.
Make vermicelli rice by frying the vermicelli in butter, adding the rice and 600 ml water and cooking for 18 minutes; serve together.
Roast the chicken with 1 tbsp oil, spices and salt at 200°C for 25 minutes and shred.
Cook the onions in 4 tbsp oil for 20 minutes until soft, add the sumac, pine nuts and chicken.
Cut the breads into large rectangles, add filling and roll tightly.
Bake at 200°C for 10 minutes until crisp and serve with yogurt.
Simmer the chicken with the onion, half the spices and salt in water for 30 minutes and keep the broth.
Fry the eggplant and potato slices until golden.
Layer the chicken, eggplant, potatoes and rice tossed with the remaining spices in a pot.
Pour over broth to cover by 2 cm and cook covered on low for 35 minutes.
Rest 10 minutes, flip onto a platter and serve with almonds and yogurt.
Rub the chicken with half the spices, oil and salt and roast at 200°C for 45 minutes.
Soften the onion in the butter, add the freekeh and remaining spices for 2 minutes.
Add the stock, cover and simmer for 25 minutes.
Serve the freekeh topped with the chicken and almonds.
Bake or fry the pita squares until crisp and spread in a dish.
Warm the chickpeas with cumin, salt and a little liquid and spoon over with the chicken.
Whisk the yogurt, tahini, garlic, lemon and salt and pour over.
Fry the pine nuts in the ghee until golden.
Pour the sizzling ghee over, then sprinkle with paprika and parsley.
Marinate the beef in oil, lemon, garlic, spices, vinegar and salt for at least 1 hour.
Sear in a very hot pan in batches for 2 minutes until charred at the edges.
Toss the parsley and onion with sumac and salt for a salad.
Serve the beef with toum, pickles, tomatoes, salad and bread.
Mix the beef with onion, parsley, spices and salt and press into a baking tray.
Bake at 200°C for 15 minutes and drain off the fat.
Layer the potatoes over the meat.
Whisk the tahini, lemon, garlic, salt and 150 ml water and pour over.
Bake 20 minutes more and scatter with toasted pine nuts.
lean halal beef or lamb mince
Knead the bulgur with 300 g of the mince, half the onion, spice and salt into a smooth paste.
Fry the rest of the mince with the remaining onion and pine nuts for the filling.
Shape the paste into shells, fill, seal into small balls and fry for 4 minutes until browned.
Whisk the yogurt with cornflour, egg and salt and heat slowly, stirring in one direction, until simmering, then add the kibbeh for 10 minutes.
Fry the garlic and mint in the butter and pour over before serving.
lean halal lamb or beef mince
Knead the bulgur with 450 g of the mince, one grated onion, half the spices and salt with a splash of iced water until smooth.
Fry the remaining mince with the second chopped onion, the rest of the spices, pine nuts, walnuts and molasses.
Press half the bulgur mix into a buttered tray, spread with the filling and cover with the rest, smoothing with wet hands.
Score into diamonds and pour the butter and oil over.
Bake at 200°C for 35 minutes until golden and crisp.
Mix the beef, rice, spice, oil and salt and fill the zucchini and potatoes three-quarters full.
Mix the tomato paste and tamarind with 1 l water and salt and pour over.
Stir the garlic and mint into the sauce for the last 5 minutes and serve.
Poach the chicken in the stock for 15 minutes, shred and keep the stock.
Soften the onion in the oil, add the spices and freekeh for 2 minutes.
Add the stock and simmer for 25 minutes.
Mix the beef with grated onion, cinnamon, half the spice and salt and roll into small balls.
Brown the meatballs in the oil and remove.
Soften the sliced onions, add the tomato paste, tomatoes, molasses, remaining spice and 300 ml water and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the meatballs and pine nuts and simmer for 20 minutes.
Cook the rice and serve together.
Mix the flour, yeast, salt, water and oil into a soft dough and leave to rise for 1 hour.
Mix the lamb with onion, tomatoes, molasses, spice and salt.
Divide the dough into 16 balls and flatten into small rounds.
Top with the meat, pressing to the edges, and scatter with pine nuts.
Bake at 230°C for 12 minutes and serve with lemon.
Simmer the lamb with the onion and salt for 90 minutes, shred and keep the broth.
Toast the nuts in a little butter, add the rice and spices, then 600 ml broth and cook for 15 minutes, adding the peas at the end.
Mix in the lamb and nuts.
Line small bowls with buttered filo, fill with the rice and fold the pastry over to seal, then turn out onto a tray.
Brush with butter and bake at 190°C for 25 minutes until golden.
Brown the beef with the onion in the oil, add the tomato paste, tomatoes, spice and 600 ml water and simmer for 60 minutes.
Fry the okra briefly in a separate pan for 4 minutes.
Add the okra and molasses to the stew and simmer for 20 minutes.
Fry the garlic and coriander and stir in.
Fry the beef, onion, pine nuts and spice in 1 tbsp oil for 8 minutes and fill the zucchini.
Fry the stuffed zucchini in the remaining oil for 5 minutes to colour.
Whisk the yogurt with cornflour, egg and salt and heat slowly, stirring in one direction, until simmering.
Add the zucchini and simmer for 20 minutes.
Fry the garlic and mint in a little oil, pour over and serve with rice.
Fry the smoked beef strips in the oil until crisp and remove, then brown the beef cubes in batches.
Soften the onion, carrots and garlic, stir in the tomato paste and flour.
Add the grape juice, balsamic vinegar, which give depth without alcohol, stock and herbs, return the beef and simmer covered for 2.5 hours.
Brown the mushrooms and pearl onions in the butter and add with the crisp strips for the last 30 minutes.
Steam the potatoes for 20 minutes and serve with the stew.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour, whisk in the milk and cook until thick, then season with nutmeg and salt.
Spread two bread slices with mustard, add turkey, a little béchamel and half the cheese, and top with the other slices.
Spread the tops with the remaining béchamel and cheese.
Bake at 220°C for 10 minutes, then grill for 2 minutes until bubbling.
Dress the salad with oil and vinegar and serve alongside.
Line a 23 cm tart tin with the pastry, chill, then blind-bake at 190°C for 15 minutes and 5 minutes more without beans.
Fry the turkey and onion for 6 minutes until golden.
Whisk the eggs, yolks, cream, milk, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Scatter the turkey and cheese in the case and pour over the custard.
Bake at 170°C for 30 minutes until just set and rest 10 minutes.
Cook the onions in the butter and oil on low for 45 minutes, stirring, until deep brown and jammy, adding the sugar halfway.
Stir in the flour, then the stock, vinegar, thyme and bay leaves.
Ladle into ovenproof bowls, top with toast and cheese and grill until bubbling.
Brown the beef with onion and garlic, add the tomato paste, stock and herbs and simmer for 15 minutes.
Boil the potatoes and mash with butter, warm milk, nutmeg, salt and pepper until smooth.
Spread the beef in a dish and cover with the purée.
Bake at 200°C for 25 minutes until golden.
Fry the eggplant in half the oil until golden and remove, then the zucchini and peppers.
Soften the onion and garlic in the remaining oil, add the tomatoes and herbs and simmer for 10 minutes.
Return the vegetables, cover and cook gently for 30 minutes.
Season and stir in torn basil.
Serve warm with crumbled goat cheese and bread.
Cover the chicken with cold water, bring to a simmer, skim, then add the onion, carrots, herbs and salt and simmer for 35 minutes.
Cook the mushrooms and pearl onions in a little butter and stock until tender.
Melt the remaining butter, stir in the flour and whisk in 700 ml of the strained stock until smooth.
Off the heat, whisk in the crème fraîche, egg yolk and lemon juice, then return the chicken, carrots, mushrooms and onions.
Warm gently without boiling and serve with rice.
Season the chicken and brown skin-side down in the oil for 8 minutes, then turn and remove.
Soften the onion and garlic, add the tomatoes, herbs and stock.
Return the chicken, cover and simmer for 25 minutes.
Add the olives and capers and cook uncovered 10 minutes.
Finish with basil and serve with bread or rice.
Chill the beef well and chop very finely by hand.
Mix with shallots, capers, gherkins, mustard, worcestershire, oil, parsley, salt and pepper.
Fry the potatoes at 160°C for 6 minutes, rest, then at 190°C for 3 minutes until crisp, and salt.
Shape the tartare into two rounds and top each with an egg yolk.
Serve immediately with the fries (use only very fresh beef from a trusted halal butcher).
halal duck fat or olive oil
Rub the duck legs with coarse salt, garlic and thyme and refrigerate overnight.
Rinse, pat dry and cover with the melted fat in a small dish.
Cook at 140°C for 2.5 hours until very tender.
Toss the potatoes in 3 tbsp of the fat with salt and roast at 220°C for 35 minutes; crisp the duck skin-side down in a hot pan for 5 minutes.
Serve the duck with potatoes, parsley and salad.
